stories.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
stories.body: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

stories.title: Four midterms takeaways for 2028 White House race
stories.body: The buzz about the presidential election is already under way - here's what we learned this week.

stories.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
stories.body: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.

stories.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
stories.body: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

stories.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
stories.body: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

stories.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
stories.body: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.

stories.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's massive arch after federal agency approval
stories.body: The Trump administration had hoped the construction of the 250-foot arch could begin as early as this week.

stories.title: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
stories.body: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.

stories.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
stories.body: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

stories.title: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
stories.body: Jim Messina tells the BBC that after Democrats' midterm victories he's talked to "over two dozen campaigns", with some already hiring staff.

stories.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
stories.body: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.

stories.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
stories.body: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.

stories.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
stories.body: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

stories.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
stories.body: Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November, satellite images suggest.

stories.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
stories.body: California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US.

stories.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
stories.body: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.

stories.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
stories.body: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".

stories.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
stories.body: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.

stories.title: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
stories.body: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.

stories.title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
stories.body: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.

However, the contested nature of some signals, coupled with the persistence of background noise, highlights the fragility of these trajectories. Governance-oriented actions are emerging as a key theme, but their sustainability will depend on broader societal buy-in and institutional resilience.

**What to watch next:** Monitor for follow-on actions in California, such as legislative or public responses to the commutations, to gauge the durability of this reform. In Somalia, track whether the judiciary’s decision leads to broader political stabilization or further conflict.
